fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Urgathoa](/Deities.aspx?ID=19)
(Pallid Princess)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="NE" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
</traits>

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 440

The chosen of Urgathoa do not dread the flaws of mortal flesh, such as aging, disease, or even death, for so long as they indulge in excess above all else, their goddess offers eternal freedom from such fickle constraints. Urgathoa herself was once a mortal woman who challenged and rejected the tenets of deities whose followers expected mindless conformity, temperance, and restraint. Why would the gods craft Golarion into a near-endless buffet abundant with pleasures of the body and mind if the living weren’t destined to feast from it? Urgathoa so loved satiating her life’s appetites that in death, she spat in the face of [Pharasma’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) judgment, murdered the psychopomp assigned to aid her transition to the afterlife, and tore herself from the Boneyard with a feat of will that not only returned her to the Material Plane but also transformed her into the first divine undead creature.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Gods of the Inner Sea](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=1)

**Edicts** become undead upon death, create or protect the undead, sate your appetites

**Anathema** deny your appetites, destroy undead, sacrifice your life

**Area of Concern**
disease, gluttony, and undeath

**Follower Alignments**
LE, NE, CE

</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>
<title level="2">Devotee Benefits</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**[Divine Attribute](/Backgrounds.aspx?ID=132)**
Constitution or Wisdom

**Divine Font** [Harm](/Spells.aspx?ID=146)

**Divine Sanctification**  can choose unholy

**Divine Skill** [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7)

**Favored Weapon** [Scythe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=39)

**Domains** [Indulgence](/Domains.aspx?ID=16), [Magic](/Domains.aspx?ID=19), [Might](/Domains.aspx?ID=20), [Undeath](/Domains.aspx?ID=34)

**[Alternate Domains](/Rules.aspx?ID=802)** [Decay](/Domains.aspx?ID=42), [Plague](/Domains.aspx?ID=48), [Swarm](/Domains.aspx?ID=53)

**Cleric Spells**

- **1st**
[Goblin Pox](/Spells.aspx?ID=139)

- **2nd**
[False Life](/Spells.aspx?ID=108)

- **7th**
[Mask of Terror](/Spells.aspx?ID=185)

</column><title level="2">Divine Intercession</title>

Urgathoa interferes in mortal affairs to fuel her own self-gratification and obsession with observing new sensations.

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 49

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Boon** You feast on the spoils of life and death. You gain the benefits of the [irongut goblin heritage](/Heritages.aspx?ID=17), regardless of your ancestry. If you already have this heritage, the circumstance bonus increases to +4.

**Moderate Boon** Urgathoa blesses you as one of her children. You gain negative healing.

**Major Boon** When you contract contagions, you experience fever dreams filled with insight. Once afflicted with a [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), you gain the effects of [_foresight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=127) with yourself as the target until no longer afflicted with any disease.
</column>

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Curse** You must overindulge or partake in forbidden feasts before you find yourself even remotely sated. You need to eat 20 times as much food as normal to avoid [starvation](/Rules.aspx?ID=537), though you always feel hungry regardless of how much you eat. If you dine on the flesh and blood of sapient creatures, you need to eat only the normal amount of such meals and your hunger abates.

**Moderate Curse** Urgathoa cuts you off from positive energy without granting you the blessing of undeath. You are harmed by positive effects and don’t recover Hit Points from them, as if you were an undead or had negative healing, but you are still harmed by negative effects as normal.

**Major Curse** Urgathoa teaches you that pointless lives in slavery to death and morality are bound to end in tragedy. You develop an incurable wasting disease that leaves you [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), and unable to move except by [Crawling](/Actions.aspx?ID=76). This disease never progresses further to kill you, but it passes to your friends and loved ones merely by sight, wasting them away unto death before your eyes and causing them to rise as undead to haunt you.
</column>

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Uskyeria](/Deities.aspx?ID=485)
(The Saintly Slumberer)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 310

Whether consciously or not, every successful hunter knows that a balance must be struck between observation and action, preparation and instinct, life and death. Taking more from the land than what is sustainable entices predators to be bolder, possibly turning the hunter into the hunted. Those who seek harmony while they live off the land give deference to Uskyeria, who urges her followers to embrace this equilibrium. Death is a natural part of life. Predators hunt prey. Those who are best suited to do so will survive. Those who don’t still feed the circle of life.

Appearing as a gigantic red [bear](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=370) with gold-streaked fur, Uskyeria is said to have originated in the far north of Avistan, between the realms currently known as Irrisen and the Sarkoris Scar. Also known as the Saintly Slumberer, this [agathion](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=216) empyreal lord’s invisible servitors bring restful sleep to both predator and prey, so they can awake refreshed upon the morn to begin the cycle anew. Insomniacs far from nature who seek balance in their own lives also pray to Uskyeria. Seeing their hunt for strength and balance just as deserving, she sometimes blesses them with the rest they so desperately need.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Empyreal Lords](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=10)

**Edicts** Preserve and protect natural resources, respect the animals you kill and their spirits, sleep as long as you need to in order to have strength for the day

**Anathema** Kill animals for reasons other than self-defense or sustenance, over-hunt the land, prevent others from getting as much sleep as they want

**Area of Concern**
Hunting, insomniacs, prudence, slumber

</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>
<title level="2">Devotee Benefits</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**[Divine Attribute](/Backgrounds.aspx?ID=132)**

**Divine Font** [Harm](/Spells.aspx?ID=146) or [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148)

fields.text: Deity Uskyeria (The Saintly Slumberer) Source Divine Mysteries pg. 310 Whether consciously or not, every successful hunter knows that a balance must be struck between observation and action, preparation and instinct, life and death. Taking more from the land than what is sustainable entices predators to be bolder, possibly turning the hunter into the hunted. Those who seek harmony while they live off the land give deference to Uskyeria, who urges her followers to embrace this equilibrium. Death is a natural part of life. Predators hunt prey. Those who are best suited to do so will survive. Those who don’t still feed the circle of life. Appearing as a gigantic red bear with gold-streaked fur, Uskyeria is said to have originated in the far north of Avistan, between the realms currently known as Irrisen and the Sarkoris Scar. Also known as the Saintly Slumberer, this agathion empyreal lord’s invisible servitors bring restful sleep to both predator and prey, so they can awake refreshed upon the morn to begin the cycle anew. Insomniacs far from nature who seek balance in their own lives also pray to Uskyeria. Seeing their hunt for strength and balance just as deserving, she sometimes blesses them with the rest they so desperately need. **Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 314

From a bacchanal gallery of gloried names remembered fondly, Ussharassim bids all who crave the warm embrace of fame, heroism, and renown to join the revelry. His kind are the young farmers who look over the glade dreaming of bards telling how they vanquished a great foe, the fiddlers who pray someone will play their song in a hundred years’ time, the adventurer who wished everyone knew their name and smiled. Hopes for grand adventure are met with the demise of their loved ones, spurning on their campaign of revenge. Poets are gifted heartbreaks that rattle their core and inspire refrains that will be quoted for generations, the glory and honor of which are indebted to the Spurring Scar forever. From his table, surrounded by heroes, villains, and masters of their time, he shares tales of all who would be the next greats, his voice crystal clear from behind a mirror mask covering a scarred visage.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Valani](/Deities.aspx?ID=486)
(The Fireshaker)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 310

Some things are constantly changing, and Valani teaches that an island is the greatest example of major changes. An island can be born from nothing, rising up from boiling waters. Over time, the hardened volcanic rock transforms into an island full of life. A powerful storm or more volcanic activity can wipe away all this life, leaving the island again bare for new change and transformation. Valani teaches embracing these changes and taking them in stride. The only way to find joy is to take each moment for what it is, and embrace all the changes that come. Valani holds great power over natural forces like storms and especially volcanoes. As such, he sees worship from [druids](/Classes.aspx?ID=34), elementalists, and people living on islands vulnerable to major changes from such primal forces. 

Valani himself is a massive [boar](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=372)-headed figure who wears a crown of spiked grass and purple flowers. His muscular body is encased in armor made from natural fibers that’s as tough as star-forged adamantine. Fireshaker is a creature of great emotional range. It is said that his laughter is strong enough to make tropical trees dance and give up their fruits to those in need, but his quickly found rage is so full of wrath that it can cleave peninsulas from their shores and cause island volcanoes to erupt for months on end. When pleased, his natural forces avoid destroying settlements or majorly disrupting lives. When upset, his storms topple homes and volcanic eruptions destroy hunting grounds, but never to such a degree that mortals can’t adapt to a new life, growing and thriving afterward.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Vale](/Deities.aspx?ID=551)
(The Court of Ancestors)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

When souls are judged in [Pharasma’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=290) court, the [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher Vale serves as the [Boneyard’s](/Planes.aspx?ID=39) chief prosecutor. They judge mortals on their actions and the impact their actions have on the world, disregarding their thoughts, beliefs, and even intentions. To Vale, a mortal only proves themselves good or evil through deeds enacted and choices made; there is no kernel of innate purity or corruption within a mortal soul, and no change wrought upon the multiverse from the privacy of the heart or mind.

Vale was created when the first wave of the River of Souls crashed against the Boneyard, carrying the cosmic weight of all mortal cultures and the influence their cultures wrought upon their hearts. They are called the Court of Ancestors, as they are the usher of consequences, superstitions, and mortal traditions, gathering and safeguarding knowledge of life on the Universe. They also care for the souls of mortals whose faith was dedicated to concepts or philosophies unrelated to the gods. Their worshippers include storytellers and those currently mourning a great loss, and they construct temples or pray to the usher in archives, courthouses, next to gallows, and before their hearths.

fields.text: Deity Vale (The Court of Ancestors) Source Divine Mysteries pg. 316 When souls are judged in Pharasma’s court, the psychopomp usher Vale serves as the Boneyard’s chief prosecutor. They judge mortals on their actions and the impact their actions have on the world, disregarding their thoughts, beliefs, and even intentions. To Vale, a mortal only proves themselves good or evil through deeds enacted and choices made; there is no kernel of innate purity or corruption within a mortal soul, and no change wrought upon the multiverse from the privacy of the heart or mind. Vale was created when the first wave of the River of Souls crashed against the Boneyard, carrying the cosmic weight of all mortal cultures and the influence their cultures wrought upon their hearts. They are called the Court of Ancestors, as they are the usher of consequences, superstitions, and mortal traditions, gathering and safeguarding knowledge of life on the Universe. They also care for the souls of mortals whose faith was dedicated to concepts or philosophies unrelated to the gods. Their worshippers include storytellers and those currently mourning a great loss, and they construct temples or pray to the usher in archives, courthouses, next to gallows, and before their hearths. <row gap="medium">

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 130

The Answering Rite is the primordial inevitable of ceremonies, magic, and preparation. Valmallos takes the form of a mechanical giant, his chest open to expose a glowing heart, with scrolls swirling about him like serpents. Valmallos understands all the laws of magic, and sends his agents against those who have acquired magical ability that they have neither earned nor have the discipline to control. Many scholars of magic believe Valmallos is at least partly responsible for the complex material, somatic, and verbal components necessary to perform magic. His followers are spellcasters who seek perfection in the performance and effects of their magic. Though willing to teach magic to others, they cloak their techniques in layers of ritual to weed out those who lack the patience to handle magic properly.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Vapula](/Deities.aspx?ID=532)
(The Exchequer)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 314

With a greed that rivals that of the oldest [dragons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=395), Vapula relishes knowledge. He particularly savors the moment when one learns something new and has to recontextualize everything as their reality changes. In the chase for revelation, he has acquired quite the collection and developed a knack for cataloging and security. All that is lost is found in his vaults. The prayers of the widower who lost his ring, the pup whose human forgot them, the knight whose sword was knocked into the crevasse in their most dire hour—their quiet offers cross the Keeper of the Pyrite Vault’s ears before any others. For easy favors, wishes can come true. [Devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=389), [demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387), archmagi, and scores of [angels](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=359) come to account with Vapula, each knowing any treasures or threats they deposit are safe and accounted for. Threats from [Asmodeus](/Deities.aspx?ID=278) himself could not ply Vapula, for the Exchequer’s word is his bond, and he is all the more respected for it. Those that meet with Vapula encounter a living stone statue of a horned man wearing an elegant robe, his visage changing every time one looks away.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Varg](/Deities.aspx?ID=561)
(The Iron Warrior)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 318

Varg is another of the older orc deities and is said to be the first [orc](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=66) to learn how to forge blades. In life, Varg was a notably intelligent orc who focused exclusively on waging war. He recognized that the orcs’ enemies were better equipped, better trained, and used better tactics in battle. He sought to learn these things, which allowed him to become a prestigious warlord. However, Varg’s experience in combat was against other orcs. His overconfidence led him to lay “siege” to a walled city outside Belkzen. The siege didn’t last long. In fact, Varg died quickly and his hold scattered.

Before every battle, Varg was known to declare his Deathright. When he succeeded at his Crucible, he spent a great deal of time studying mortals and how they waged war. Siege engines caught his attention, and he gave the secrets of building them to his mortal brethren. Orcs often use these weapons of war to pay homage to the Iron Warrior, but a number see the use of technology for anything other than combat as blasphemy.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Vavaalrav](/Deities.aspx?ID=552)
(The Steeple’s Skull)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

Mortals have always needed ways to remember and honor their ancestors, and it was from this fundamental need the [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher Vavaalrav first imagined the spires and steeples of the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39). Vavaalrav is the guardian of sacred places, and the chill of his breath and stillness of his presence is felt across every mausoleum, tomb, and other burial ground of [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26). The Steeple’s Skull does not tolerate when the sanctity of a holy site or the rest of the dead is disturbed, and his symbol is used by mortals to ward graves against foul spirits and grave robbers alike.

The psychopomp’s cult attracts mortal architects, groundskeepers, mortuary workers, and masons, as well as many gargoyles. Even when they don’t worship the usher of graves, [gargoyles](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=49) whose perches adorn cathedrals, temples, and tombs pay Vavaalrav the respect he is due as patron and protector of the hallowed grounds they call home.

Vavaalrav’s home, the Wailing Tor, is an impressive spire at the center of the Boneyard’s Eight Courts. Within its walls, all souls find the peace and rest of the afterlife, and the usher takes special care to welcome and watch over spirits who struggled to accept their fate and leave their mortal lives behind.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Velgaas](/Deities.aspx?ID=601)
(Minds in the Dark)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 320

Many an idealist with great hopes to change the world has had their dreams realized by meeting a handsome stranger on the road. Velgaas, who might be mistaken for a [nagaji](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=54) with his scaled skin and forked tongue, takes great care to learn their altruistic desires, then carefully plants the seeds of destruction into their kind hearts. Charities become cesspools of corruption, laboratories convert into dens of torture, and peaceful protests spiral into mob violence. 

Velgaas is the most methodical of the sahkil tormentors, preying on good intentions to fulfill his own evil designs. He rules over the aspects of emotional manipulation, emptiness, and ignorance, carefully selecting each word and action to best ingratiate himself with an unsuspecting victim. A honeyed tongue is his weapon, a mask of sincerity his shield. Few of the unfortunate souls who cross his path would ever believe how deeply he’s manipulated them. 

Corrupt politicians and courtiers are among Velgaas’s followers, but he prizes most the ones who fall into his hands unknowingly. The well-meaning authorities he influences might crack down on crime by way of an oppressive city guard or falsify evidence to finally execute a dangerous criminal.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Sakhil Tormentors](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=31)

**Edicts** Be sweet with lies and cruel with truths, corrupt the good intentions of others, master the art of manipulation

**Anathema** Be obvious with your lies, reveal the truth without benefit

**Area of Concern**
Emotional manipulation, emptiness, ignorance

fields.text: Deity Velgaas (Minds in the Dark) Source Divine Mysteries pg. 320 Many an idealist with great hopes to change the world has had their dreams realized by meeting a handsome stranger on the road. Velgaas, who might be mistaken for a nagaji with his scaled skin and forked tongue, takes great care to learn their altruistic desires, then carefully plants the seeds of destruction into their kind hearts. Charities become cesspools of corruption, laboratories convert into dens of torture, and peaceful protests spiral into mob violence. Velgaas is the most methodical of the sahkil tormentors, preying on good intentions to fulfill his own evil designs. He rules over the aspects of emotional manipulation, emptiness, and ignorance, carefully selecting each word and action to best ingratiate himself with an unsuspecting victim. A honeyed tongue is his weapon, a mask of sincerity his shield. Few of the unfortunate souls who cross his path would ever believe how deeply he’s manipulated them. Corrupt politicians and courtiers are among Velgaas’s followers, but he prizes most the ones who fall into his hands unknowingly. The well-meaning authorities he influences might crack down on crime by way of an oppressive city guard or falsify evidence to finally execute a dangerous criminal. <title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">

(Most Glorious Neverfull)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 312

Among [goblins](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=62), Venkelvore is considered the most beautiful of gods. Many goblins depict her as a fellow goblin rather than her true form: a [barghest](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=11) with pale blue fur and a trio of tails. Venkelvore has an eternal hunger that’s only satiated by consuming her enemies. She prefers to eat her meals while still alive, as she not only feeds on the meat but also the prey’s suffering, which Venkelvore considers a fantastic side dish. 

Among the many ways to venerate Venkelvore, her followers believe that the best way to impress her is by tying up as many prisoners as they can during raids and burning them alive, savoring them as they cook or as part of a celebration once the pillaging ends. Her high priests say that the screams of agony please Venkelvore, who rewards those who follow her with more teeth, or sharpening their teeth and claws, allowing these followers to eat their next meal with greater ease.

Goblins who venerate the Most Glorious Neverfull sometimes worship [Lurlup](/Deities.aspx?ID=504) as well. They dedicate their lives to eating everything they can, trying to satiate the hunger of both of their gods. These voracious individuals tend to live isolated lives, as most other goblins tend to find their habits off-putting.

Verilorn, Lord of Wood, Custodian of Oak and Ash, is a gardener. While some might consider gardening to be a free-flowing form of creation, Verilorn believes his gardens should be orderly and exact above all else. Verilorn knows when a sprout will form into wood with such nicety that even the deities who govern time take inspiration.

Verilorn, Custodian of Oak and Ash, is the elemental lord of wood, cultivation, and forestry. His creations now are physically perfect, but ideologically cold.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Vermilion Mother](/Deities.aspx?ID=602)
(The Endless Root)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries Web Supplement](/Sources.aspx?ID=237) pg. 21

A rare few of those who’ve indulged in psychoactive plants have been met with horrifying visions of an old woman made of gnarled vines and roots, her sneering mouth full of fang-like thorns and pollen. Those unfortunate enough to meet Vermilion Mother are stalked in their sleep, choked nightly by her dream of a world overrun by plants and fungi. This sahkil tormentor cares little for those of flesh and blood, only that their bodies make for excellent fertilizer.

The Endless Root is worshipped by creatures with a strong preference for nature over civilization, pointing to industry and urbanization as roots of crime and pollution. She doesn’t care for worship but accepts it as a way to promote growth and propagation, enlisting her followers to protect plant life of all kinds. She is one of the few sahkil tormentors to have followers who don’t live wicked lifestyles, some of them even believing themselves benevolent as they work to keep nature unspoiled. But more often than not, her followers are fanatically devoted to the protection of plants to the point of killing anyone they judge as harmful to their territory, using them as sacrifices to feed the undergrowth.

</title>

<row gap="medium">

<trait label="LG" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 128

The Cardinal Martyr presides over devotion, sacrifice, and scars. Vildeis is driven entirely by her abhorrence for evil. Evil should not and must not be allowed to exist. It should be fought without pause and without rest until it is completely and utterly destroyed. Not only does the fight never end, but every sacrifice that needs to be made to end evil must be made, and is worth making. There are no material rewards to be had for destroying evil—its destruction is all the reward necessary, and that reward can be enjoyed only once there is no more evil. Scars are the marks the fight leaves behind, the memory of all the sacrifices made. Vildeis expects total commitment from her followers, who leave everything behind and dedicate their lives to destroying all that is vile.

 The Cardinal Martyr appears as a human woman covered in scars, each forming a rune depicting a sacrifice she has made. Her eyes are covered in a red cloth so that she cannot see the horrors of evil upon the world. Vildeis flies on gigantic, blood-colored wings, and the whispered screams of all the planes’ martyrs can be heard in her presence. Followers of Vildeis include martyrs, paladins, and zealots.

fields.text: Deity Vildeis (The Cardinal Martyr) LG Source Gods & Magic pg. 128 The Cardinal Martyr presides over devotion, sacrifice, and scars. Vildeis is driven entirely by her abhorrence for evil. Evil should not and must not be allowed to exist. It should be fought without pause and without rest until it is completely and utterly destroyed. Not only does the fight never end, but every sacrifice that needs to be made to end evil must be made, and is worth making. There are no material rewards to be had for destroying evil—its destruction is all the reward necessary, and that reward can be enjoyed only once there is no more evil. Scars are the marks the fight leaves behind, the memory of all the sacrifices made. Vildeis expects total commitment from her followers, who leave everything behind and dedicate their lives to destroying all that is vile. The Cardinal Martyr appears as a human woman covered in scars, each forming a rune depicting a sacrifice she has made. Her eyes are covered in a red cloth so that she cannot see the horrors of evil upon the world. Vildeis flies on gigantic, blood-colored wings, and the whispered screams of all the planes’ martyrs can be heard in her presence. Followers of Vildeis include martyrs, paladins, and zealots. <title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Vineshvakhi](/Deities.aspx?ID=262)
(The Pain of Purity)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="LN" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
</traits>

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 319

In the pursuit of righteousness, one will suffer 10,000 little deaths. Those of purity will accept this torment and emerge knowing every danger the world might cast upon them, while those who flee like cowards from their task will know only their mortality. This truth was first claimed by Vineshvakhi, who even as a fledgling divinity couldn't begin to appreciate the gravity of his charge until he suffered pain and humiliation in its defense.

 In ancient days, Vineshvakhi was tasked with protecting a blessed vault. Whatever it contained, Vineshvakhi knew only that he was to protect it, that he was never to look upon it, and that the asuras in all their blasphemous horror would seek to steal it. The raid by the asuras was a three-pronged attack. Vineshvakhi bested waves of fiendish horrors, resolute in his actions and unwilling to give an inch of ground or willpower to their corrupting devices. He turned the tide against Gavidya the Numberless's hordes, and struck true against Taraksun the Wakener of Wrath. The skies in Heaven were an erupting cacophony of brilliant lights, crashing blades, and fiendish miasma; in the end, it was Bohga who won the day. The Treasurer rana warped Vineshvakhi's own hand to remove the lock. Unwilling to cede any ground, the god of guardians severed each of his six fingers and spat in the eye of the rana.

 Throughout the Impossible Lands, the ramifications of this conflict still carry forth. Calikangs were born from these divine fallen fingers and seek greater communion with the father they feel they failed when they were still part of his flesh. Ever resurgent, so too do asuras remain in dire numbers, pursuing the death of the divine. Wanderers of Vineshvakhi's order, the virajvinesh serve as sacred bodyguards, fiend hunters, and sacred slayers second only to the clerics of [Abadar](/Deities.aspx?ID=1) in their devotion to protection as a blessed concept.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Other Gods](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=2)

**Edicts** protect holy people, places, and treasures; sacrifice common comforts and mortal joys for the sake of your charge

**Anathema** abandon your post, fail to protect your charge, willingly suffer corruption over death or grievous harm

**Area of Concern**
guardians, locks, sacrifice, vaults

**Follower Alignments**
LG, LN

</column>

</column>

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Vonymos](/Deities.aspx?ID=553)
(The Mourning Storm)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

Grief is a powerful emotion, felt by every mortal in every lifetime, and from the pain of intense loss crashing through mortal hearts a [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher was born: Vonymos, the Mourning Storm. They embody all that grows from a heart in mourning, both good and ill. They are depression, isolation, and desperation, but they are also last stands against the dark, renewed vigor, and hope. The usher’s touch is felt when emotions swell, building up until they grow too overwhelming to contain, when the walls within crumble and the flood is unleashed. They are the crack of lighting that pushes mortals through despair, igniting the inner fire needed to make a final, desperate rally before succumbing to defeat. They are the usher of catastrophes, of last stands, and of suicides.

Vonymos is worshipped by mortal bards, counselors, and crusaders, who gather in abandoned tombs and erect great circles of standing stones over mass graves. In the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39), the usher tends to souls of those who fall to suicide, martyrdom, and catastrophes, while their cult offers solace and comfort to those left behind on [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26).

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 302

Vorasha is considered the most powerful of the daemonic harbingers likely because of her close ties to [Trelmarixian](/Deities.aspx?ID=137), the Rider of Famine. Some say that he has had a subtle influence on the Ophidian’s rise through the ranks. However, Vorasha has plans of her own to become a Rider in her own right, focusing on poisons and incurable toxins. She schemes from the Writhing Palace, a vast garden of poisonous plants infested with venomous serpents. Because this domain lies wholly within the Withered Court, Trelmarixian’s realm, Vorasha suspects the Rider of Famine is aware of her every move. 

Vorasha appears as a scaled draconic humanoid with clawed hands and feet. She has a tangle of scarlet-and-emerald snakes as hair that are constantly writhing. As the Lady of Toxicity, she wears a flowing green gown that drips with poisons.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Vudravati](/Deities.aspx?ID=359)
(The Peaceful Mother)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 161

According to the _Mizravratta Brahmodya_, in the days when Golarion had not yet finished forming, the god Vudravati wandered across the still-changing landscapes, breathing her joy and wonder into creation. Twin brothers, the gods [Embaral](/Deities.aspx?ID=340) and [Obari](/Deities.aspx?ID=356), fell in love with her and both wished to please her. She loved them both and rejoiced in their company. But the brothers, unable to understand her boundless generosity, grew jealous, each wanting to control her love. They tried to force Vudravati into choosing between them, but she refused. Turning to violence, each brother then reasoned that, by destroying his twin, he would at last have all of Vudravati’s love for himself. An epic battle began that threatened to reshape the nascent world as the brothers toppled mountains, tore open vast canyons, and raised hurricanes, all in the hopes of destroying the other. 

At first, Vudravati despaired, feeling despondent and powerless in the face of such willful and widespread destruction. Her love seemed pointless, and she could find no rest, so anguished was she by their aggression. Why had they not seen the generosity of her love? Did they really love her? Eventually, she decided to put this last question to the test. Vudravati called the brothers to her and convinced them to call a truce so that she could get some sleep. Each agreed only if she would lie down with him. So, she stretched out between the two, putting an end to their fighting. 

As she went to sleep, Vudravati transformed into the land now known as Vudra. The two brothers, realizing their foolishness, became embodied in the Obari Ocean to the southwest and the Embaral Ocean to the east. From her body, says the scripture, emerged the people of Vudra, and she continues to support their every need through land and river. Many Vudrani believe they owe everything to her and ought to show her the utmost respect as she continues to sleep. In return, they say that she will continue to shower her people with her generous gifts and calm the twin oceans’ destructive rage. These worshippers see Vudravati as quite literally their land, raising simple shrines of natural materials and offering prayers to her spirit as it rests in the earth.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Vulot](/Deities.aspx?ID=439)
(The All or None)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 304

Vulot is the nascent demon lord of lies, loss of identity, and suffocation. The All or None receives worship from liars, con artists, opportunistic community leaders, and even some stage performers. As befits a demon lord of disguises and swapping faces, Vulot has several forms, varying from a [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) body made up of dozens of different faces to a nondescript, mannequin-like form with no face at all. The All or None sees each identity stolen as an opportunity to consume the potential that individual holds. Vulot doesn’t feed on the abstract idea of potential, instead using a person’s potential to provide divine fuel for further machinations. Vulot’s ultimate goal is to use all of this potential to ascend far beyond the status of demon lord into something greater, destroying or appropriating anyone else along the way, including any fellow demon lords that may act as obstacles to this goal. The demon lord’s cultists tend to be individual and solitary, as covering up their identity requires few to know their true selves. Their work aims less for direct confrontation instead destroying the connections of a community through falsehoods and whisper campaigns. Luckily, the All or None’s followers are generally too individualistic for more than short-term gains.

[Walkena](/Deities.aspx?ID=159)
(The God-King)
</title>

<row gap="medium">

</traits>

**Source** [The Mwangi Expanse](/Sources.aspx?ID=89) pg. 143

In the city-state of Mzali in the Mwangi Expanse resides an undead being of immense power, a child-sized god-king. </title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 241

Life-giving water is an important building block for most civilizations. It’s needed to fill wells, irrigate farms, and facilitate the movement of goods. It’s the reason many of the world’s most prosperous cities are built on coasts and riverbanks. Many find this fact worthy of reverence, but don’t wish to pay obeisance to any particular ocean or river god. They put their faith in the water itself, often personified in spirits and elementals of the [Plane of Water](/Planes.aspx?ID=32). Followers of the Waves of the Boundless Sea also respect the sheer power of the ocean and the ceaseless but ultimately predictable tides. Many go through life drifting on the currents of fate, letting circumstances carry them like a river to the sea. Others understand that while waves might toss and capsize a ship, water not tossed by the winds should be more calming and regularly bathe or soak themselves for therapeutic purposes.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Weight of the World](/Deities.aspx?ID=384)

</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 245

All things gravitate toward equilibrium, but this is not the same thing as balance. Nature is constantly shifting and changing. When new growth becomes old, it is broken down to become raw materials for new things once more. Those who are closest to the land know this the best. Volcanoes erupt and destroy, but then make the earth on and near their slopes so much more fertile afterward... until they erupt anew.

People who have studied or survived natural disasters or extreme weather events also know this far too well. By making sacrifices and offerings to the deities who embody primal forces and changes, they gain a better understanding of how to harness these energies for themselves. Those who venerate the Weight of the World are usually spellcasters, but sometimes scholars who look for patterns and meaning in the natural world’s cycles also seek a bit of divine inspiration in their quest for knowledge.

</title>

<row gap="medium">

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 245

If necessity is the proverbial mother of invention, it can also count creativity, curiosity, inspiration, and hard work among its forebears. The divine entities of the Wheels of Innovation share a passion for motivating those who seek to breathe new life and fresh ideas into their fields of creation. These gods of invention and artistry currently believe the formation of this pantheon is their greatest idea to date. 

Worship of this pantheon originated in urban centers around Golarion’s Inner Sea region and in nations like Alkenstar, Numeria, and Rahadoum. Recently, it has also begun to blossom in more rural communities, as its adherents try to solve physical problems without relying on spellcasters or government officials. This has most firmly taken root in [gnome](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=61), [goblin](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=62), and [halfling](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=63) communities. Many of them profess that tinkering and experimentation are a far more positive—but no less exciting—way to seek entertainment as well.

fields.text: Deity Wheels of Innovation Source Divine Mysteries pg. 245 If necessity is the proverbial mother of invention, it can also count creativity, curiosity, inspiration, and hard work among its forebears. The divine entities of the Wheels of Innovation share a passion for motivating those who seek to breathe new life and fresh ideas into their fields of creation. These gods of invention and artistry currently believe the formation of this pantheon is their greatest idea to date. Worship of this pantheon originated in urban centers around Golarion’s Inner Sea region and in nations like Alkenstar, Numeria, and Rahadoum. Recently, it has also begun to blossom in more rural communities, as its adherents try to solve physical problems without relying on spellcasters or government officials. This has most firmly taken root in gnome, goblin, and halfling communities. Many of them profess that tinkering and experimentation are a far more positive—but no less exciting—way to seek entertainment as well. fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Whispering Way](/Deities.aspx?ID=389)

</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 250

Life is frequently messy, complicated, and brutal. Many mortals have sought to tame the inherent chaos of existence, seeking control of their circumstances through philosophy or strictly enforced law. Yet there are existences beyond mortality; the scholars who formed the Whispering Way chose to solve the tumult life brings by snuffing it out entirely. To the Whispering Way, life holds no value: it is a wasteful state chained to constant biological needs and irrational emotions. Unfettered by such paltry concerns, the Whispering Way seeks to embrace the perfection of undeath, transcending mortal ecology and creating a utopian society free of flaws or dissent.

The Whispering Way attracts those bereft of compassion or morals, reframing these mortal vices into the virtue of rationality. It likewise draws its fair share of megalomaniacs, surprising few who know of it. It views undeath as a route to power and personal apotheosis, catapulting an adherent beyond their mortal limitations. While followers laud any state of undeath as higher than life, most adherents are self-serving enough to seek a comfortable existence as a higher form of undead, rather than a mindless drudge to the more powerful. [Liches](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=438) are idealized above all others due to the intense knowledge, courage, and magical mastery required to attain lichdom.

Death also has a way of smoothing over mortal differences. Conflicting needs, internal prejudice, and clashing cultures have a way of fading from importance once their members are plunged into the cold of undeath. The Whispering Way thus seeks to save the world, delivering it from the short-sighted clutches of those ruled by their emotions and their flickering life spans. The grim dispassion of the dead is the only solution to the impassioned selfishness of the living. While the Whispering Way is united in its proclivities, goals, and reverence for undeath, its philosophy has many branches. Just as there is no universal path to lichdom, so too are there many different views on undeath and the path to paradise. These philosophies cannot be learned from books or actions; it must only be spoken in a breathless rasp from the mouth of one to the ears of another. Tomes revealing the truths of the Whispering Way are either rambling hoaxes of the delusional or penned by the philosophy’s most hated enemies. Should word of such written lore get out, the Whispering Way is quick to hunt down these books and burn them.

The Whispering Way claims no founder, prophet, or divine muse; the Way merely is and exists as a realization to be grasped by those intelligent, realistic, insightful, and ambitious enough to fathom it. It needs history and mythology no more than do mathematical principles or physical laws, and by the same right, requires no belief to be true. Those who understand it accept it as fact and work to attain the stagnant utopia idealized at its heart. Those who instead fear it and the fundamental changes it means for the living world, would rather embrace death’s ultimate oblivion than divest themselves of the ephemeral comforts of a chaotic world. Such are the understandings of the Way, and its adherents require no greater pedigree or reason to pursue its objectives than the promise of the dark powers and immortal influence they’ll wield in the idealized corpse-world of their dream.

**Anathema** speak the secrets of the Whispering Way above a whisper, write down the philosophies of the Whispering Way, act irrationally due to concerns for the living

**Area of Concern**
undeath, lichdom, secrets

</column>

(The Bone Breaker)
</title>

<row gap="medium">

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 318

Wulgren, like [Jukha](/Deities.aspx?ID=556), is a [dromaar](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=70). He traveled exceptionally far and wide as a mortal before his ascension. Wulgren was born in Belkzen but became separated from his party during a scouting expedition. After a brief period held captive by a group of adventuring Pathfinders, Wulgren was freed on his own recognizance and traveled to Alkenstar, the City of Smog.

While in Alkenstar, Wulgren developed a great skill in weapon smithing and forged an unlikely and powerful [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16): the [barricade buster](/Weapons.aspx?ID=330). With this massive, inaccurate, but deadly weapon in hand, Wulgren swore his Deathright and returned to Belkzen to stand against the hordes of the Whispering Tyrant. During a brutal battle against an endless stream of skeletal undead, Wulgren and his mighty weapon ultimately fell, and he continued on to fight his Crucible.

It’s unclear which orc deity Wulgren slew; most likely it was another orc who had passed the Crucible previously, whose name had not yet spread widely enough to be well known. Whoever they were, Wulgren defeated them (though it’s unclear if he did so with his barricade buster or more conventional weaponry), and Wulgren the Bone-Breaker now stands proudly among Belkzen’s gods.

(The Star Seed)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="NE" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
</traits>

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 132

Xhamen-Dor, the living cancer, was born in the sewers beneath Carcosa, the alien city that is the home of [Hastur](/Deities.aspx?ID=162). Somehow, this Great Old One was transported to Golarion within a comet, crashing into the bottom of a lake during the devastation of Earthfall. Physically, it manifests as a twisting and vaguely serpentine-shaped mass of bone, hair, and fungus.

 The Inmost Blot, as Xhamen-Dor is also known, exists to conquer worlds by infecting the living with itself. Its victims, the seeded, enact its will and seek to spread its influence until the entire world is just an extension of Xhamen-Dor itself. Then, once only the seeded remain, Xhamen-Dor uses the last of the planet’s energy to return to Carcosa, which in turn absorbs the world Xhamen-Dor has brought to it, allowing Carcosa to slowly grow.

(The Flying Scab)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries Web Supplement](/Sources.aspx?ID=237) pg. 21

Trapped deep beneath the Black Pyramid of Xibalba lives an embodiment of destruction known as the Flying Scab. Few have seen Xiquiripat and lived to tell tales of their constantly shifting guise, which changes from waves of congealed blood to a knot of fanged lampreys to a heaving mass of matted hair. Though this god’s form is fluid, their goals are less so, as Xiquiripat has had only one unbending desire since the dawn of their existence: to instill fear into every living thing they meet before condemning them to oblivion.

Xiquiripat’s worshippers and clerics roam the halls of the Black Pyramid, heavily armed and eager to honor their god with violence. These followers are not exempt from their deity’s lust for annihilation, but few have had the privilege to receive death at the hands of the one they worship. Xiquiripat’s rare devotees in the Universe are those with a predilection for murder and inflicting death. Though these individuals can display a veneer of social graces and blend in with their community, any sign of blessings from Xiquiripat is a stark warning that they are indiscriminate killers incapable of remorse for the pain they wreak on others.

(Horned Prince)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 304

Xoveron jealously guards his spheres of [gargoyles](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=49), reckless consumption, and ruins. When the fourarmed, four-headed Horned Prince hunts, the air fills with the horrific sound of stone grinding on stone. The demon lord particularly exalts in the destruction of cities, encouraging people to use more resources than they contribute, while bandits that prey on cities and villages often ask for his blessing upon them and his curse on their targets. He also enjoys the ruination and suffering of architects, sculptors, and those who aim to build something lasting. Unlike most other demon lords, Xoveron has the patience for longterm disruption, as befit the venerated prince of stony gargoyles. Cults form from either the aforementioned bandits or the absurdly wealthy, who often benefit from slowly crushing of those beneath them for the slightest taste of the finest things life can offer.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Xsistaid](/Deities.aspx?ID=423)
(The Wriggling Wound)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 302

Sometimes, desperate individuals suffering in the wake of plague and illness cry out to the cosmos for aid. Xsistaid is the chittering voice attempting to convince them that their continuing survival means shedding all pretenses of goodness, and preying upon whomever is in reach, growing strong by robbing others of their vitality. The Wriggling Wound cares not that there is no honor in becoming a parasite. Only the fact that it leads to a longer life matters. 

Xsistaid’s true form is a swarming mass of multicolored parasitic fungi and maggots, from which a screaming petitioner occasionally thrashes to the surface in an attempt to escape. Usually, Xsistaid hides within the decaying body of a non-[daemon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=386) outsider (such as an [angel](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=359)), controlling the corpse’s every move.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Yaezhing](/Deities.aspx?ID=318)
(The Minister of Blood)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries Web Supplement](/Sources.aspx?ID=237) pg. 22

When the gods of the Celestial Court were given their divine duties, it was Yaezhing who was assigned the title of Minister of Blood, the punisher of the gods, and the enforcer of divine justice. When Fumeiyoshi was found guilty of murdering his brother Tsukiyo, it was Yaezhing who was tasked with burying him alive and making an example of those who would cross the Court. When assassins and executioners are hired to carry out capital punishments, it is Yaezhing who they pray to for a steady hand and the conviction to follow through.

 As the god of assassins and executioners, Yaezhing oversees contracted death and guides those who are tasked with the duty of killing others. He is also seen as a figure of justice, meting out bloody punishment to all who deserve it, whether godly or mortal. Judges and constables pray to him for criminals to be convicted and given the harshest sentences. Those who have been wronged by the corrupt courts of mortals beg Yaezhing for divine justice to be doled out by his hand. Most people and gods are wary of Yaezhing, seeing him as a necessary evil at best and a force of murderous destruction at worst. Yaezhing doesn't see a need to clear up any misunderstandings, the same way that a sword or shuriken doesn't need to explain itself to the people who wield them.

 Despite his gruesome title and task, Yaezhing does not partake in wanton murder. In his eyes, the act of killing is not done for pleasure or glory, but to fulfill a binding agreement that has been made between executioner and law or assassin and client. Once the contract is made and the payment is finalized, it becomes the sole duty of Yaezhing and his followers to bring about the death of the target.

 Yaezhing doesn't concern himself with determining who is guilty and who should live or die. For him, there is no difference between legally approved executions and contracted assassinations. They are simply two sides of the same coin, where death is the greatest equalizer, and Yaezhing is duty-bound to be its wielder and weapon.

(The Polymorph Plague)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 320

Yamasoth appears as a nightmarish octopus with a multitude of tentacles, each ending in a method of inflicting pain. His body is a single massive mouth filled with sharp teeth and stinging tongues. Eyes dot his form, and one huge red eye sits within his throat. Like all qlippoth lords, Yamasoth seeks to eradicate [demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) by eliminating sin in mortals, but his methods involve corrupting powerful leaders until they doom their kingdoms and performing terrible fleshwarping experiments on hapless victims to release monsters upon civilization. Yamasoth has a grudging respect tempered with disdain for [Lamashtu](/Deities.aspx?ID=287) for her hand in creating monsters but hates almost all other deities. 

Cultists of the Polymorph Plague tend to be immoral inventors, doctors, and torturers. They push the boundaries of what mortal bodies can withstand, not fully realizing that Yamasoth grants them their abilities to cause a disruption in the ways that mortals experience and understand sin.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Yamatsumi](/Deities.aspx?ID=319)
(The Mountain Lord)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries Web Supplement](/Sources.aspx?ID=237) pg. 22

Yamatsumi watches over his followers from high atop snowcapped mountains and volcanic peaks. From these vantage points, he can easily observe his followers work the land and set up temples and shrines to his glory on the numerous peaks that crisscross the world. At times when he is displeased at how his people have misused the fertile valleys, fed by mountain streams, Yamatsumi will remind his followers of his wrath with a minor avalanche or a belch of dark smoke from a volcano. His followers once failed to heed such warnings, and Yamatsumi caused Mount Kumijinja in Minkai to erupt mightily to demonstrate his anger, covering the continent in ash, and darkening the skies for months. While a horrific event, the tremendous heat melted the glaciers on the mountain, further feeding the rivers running through the green valleys, and the ash from the eruption provided fine fertilizer for the earth below. As such, once his wrath was satiated, the land again began to renew and grow back even more fruitful than before. Some fear such eruptions might herald a repeat of the catastrophes that caused the Age of Ashes almost 10,000 years ago, though Yamatsumi has vowed not to allow his wrath to extend that deep. Even so, his followers—from ascetic mountain monks to people from all walks of life—pray to Yamatsumi to avert his ire when the first winds of winter blow or a nearby volcano begins to smoke.

 While his presence can be felt on any mountaintop, Yamatsumi is especially pleased when followers ascend the tallest and most challenging peaks to build temples and shrines in his name. Should such followers falter altogether, Yamatsumi preserves them where they fall in solid ice, a monument to their courage.

 Priests of the Mountain Lord eschew the comforts of civilization for a life of asceticism. They seek tall peaks to build simple dwellings and sturdy temples for worship. From their lofty positions among the mountaintops, they take in the grandeur of nature, and their solitude enables them to see the pettiness of the dealings far below. When Yamatsumi chooses to appear, he does so as a giant man with ice for skin, lava for hair and a beard, and two pairs of ram's horns on his head.

</title>

<row gap="medium">

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 130

The protean lord of language evolution, lost words, and slang, Ydajisk manifests as a protean with six arms and a cobra’s hood, surrounded by a cloud of drifting sounds, symbols, shapes, and myriad other sensory experiences that shift endlessly in and out of existence. Closer inspection reveals that their body is made from interlacing strands of poetic protean script. Ydajisk is also called the Mother of Tongues, though like all proteans, their gender changes as they will. Followers of Ydajisk are wanderers, reviving dead languages from ancient ruins, chronicling the dying tongues of cultures in decline, and discovering or inventing new words. All such knowledge acquired by agents of the Mother of Tongues passes into Ydajisk’s realm, the Library of Stolen Words, where it is transcribed into books or stored in magical containers, alongside scrolls and tomes considered long lost by mortal scholars.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Yelayne](/Deities.aspx?ID=268)
(The Wind Weaver)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="NG" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
</traits>

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 68

There once was a weaver named Yelayne who was known far and wide for making the finest cloth and most beautiful garments, and one day the Wind fell in love with her. The Wind followed Yelayne everywhere, tugging on her hair and rumpling the beautiful clothing that she worked so hard to craft. She ignored him, because she was wise and knew the Wind could be fickle and cruel. When he persisted in pursuing her against her wishes, she brought out her most tightly-woven bag and whistled for the Wind's attention. When he came rushing, she trapped him in the bag. Ever afterward, she only let the Wind out if he promised to obey her. Yelayne had the Wind carry her all over the world, teaching the art of weaving to any who would work at it and learning how to make the most fantastical clothes. When she tired of that, she had the Wind carry her to [Heaven](/Planes.aspx?ID=17), where she wove starlight into constellations, sunshine into rainbows, and moonbeams into enchantments. She still watches to make sure that none are left exposed for the old Wind to bother, and that all are able to pursue their creative endeavors, express themselves, and dress how they like.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Other Gods](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=2)

**Edicts** develop a signature style, express yourself through craft, provide necessities and protection for those in need

clothing, craftspeople, security, self-expression

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Yhidothrus](/Deities.aspx?ID=441)
(The Ravager Worm)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 304

Yhidothrus is the demon lord of the horrific aspects of time: erosion, decay, entropy, the fear of aging, and worms. The Ravager Worm operates slowly, letting time do his work, as his twisting body grows ever longer. Rumored to be connected (physically and in origin) to [qlippoths](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=460), Yhidothrus’s form is an infinitely long worm with night black flesh and a mouth of a dozen jaws and countless teeth. This demon lord’s physical connection to the realm of qlippoths can also explain his slow workings; he is physically incapable of reaching into the territory of the other demon lords. His cults tend to be solitary individuals determined to avoid death and aging, transforming themselves into [liches](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=438) or other monstrosities, doing the demon lord’s work less for his power and more to avoid his reach, letting him decay other things in exchange for preserving their existence.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Yig](/Deities.aspx?ID=579)
(Father of Serpents)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 318

Known to mortals as the Father of Serpents, Yig is an outlier among Great Old Ones in that he appears, at least on the surface, to pose little threat to mortals. The truth of the matter is somewhat more complicated, however, as the serpentine god enters intermittent feeding frenzies, during which even his most devout followers know to avoid attracting his attention, lest they become his next meal. When appearing before his congregation, Yig often takes on the form of a massive serpentine being with arms and legs, covered in green scales except for a distinctive silver crescent on his brow.

Worship of the Father of Serpents is isolated almost exclusively to rural communities that rely on seasonal cycles, such as nomadic followings and farming villages, and as such very few temples exclusively dedicated to the serpent god exist. Instead, worshippers congregate in forest clearings and cave mouths to leave tribute to Yig, most often in the form of food. Despite his position as a god of [snakes](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=473), [serpentfolk](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=468) society treats Yig with irreverence as a result of his historical rivalry with the now-dead [Ydersius](/Deities.aspx?ID=323); Yig, meanwhile, pays this disdain no heed.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Ylimancha](/Deities.aspx?ID=132)
(Harborwing)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>
<trait label="NG" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
</traits>

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 128

Ylimancha gazes out over the world’s coastlines, presiding over coastal waters, fishers, and flying creatures. Also known as Harborwing, she believes in harmony between the seas, the skies, and the beings of the land. Sustenance and resources can be taken from the sea by those on shore, but not so much that the balance is upset. The sea may sometimes encroach on the land, but breakwaters can be built to keep communities on land dry and safe. Ylimancha likewise loves all creatures that fly, though the demon lord [Pazuzu](/Deities.aspx?ID=79) also claims dominion over them, bringing the two into endless conflict and causing her to mourn deeply each creature he converts to his worship.

 Harborwing most often appears as a very large seagull, pure white in color with the head of a Varisian woman with short, dark hair. She sometimes instead appears as a human woman with the head of an osprey. In this form she wears robes that sway like the waves of the sea, their blue folds foaming white at the edges, and she carries a teak longbow strung with gold. When she speaks, her voice carries the sound of the crashing waves. Followers of Ylimancha include fishers, sailors, merfolk, those who make their living on or in the sea, and flying creatures.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
[Yluma](/Deities.aspx?ID=721)
(The Living Page)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Draconic Codex](/Sources.aspx?ID=277) pg. 34

More than her kin, Yluma wielded magic with power. Magical currents coursed through her body, filling her frame with the power to raise mountains and level entire plains. Yet each awe-inspiring act came at an incredible cost. With each miraculous feat, Yluma’s form changed, becoming less distinct and whole. Yluma shared her fears with her father, but the [Waybringer](/Deities.aspx?ID=330) could do nothing to stop this change. He confided that in Yluma he could see a fragment of [Sarshallatu’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=719) infinity. Yluma’s body, no matter how powerful, would eventually be torn at the seams, unable to contain her mother’s unbound vastness. And so, Yluma vowed to seek out Sarshallatu, hoping that her mother would help her get rid of such a curse. She traveled far and wide across the edges of creation. Her frame, pulled and stretched by the trials she faced, seemed on the verge of collapse when she finally reached her mother’s lonely refuge. She gazed upon her divine mother, trying to take in all her vastness and power. Yluma looked at herself, feeling the soreness of her powerful muscles, tired and aching after the long journey. She traced the scars left by her battles, remembering how she bested all those who opposed her using her gifts. And she understood. 

So, she returned to her kin, her body a monument to her triumphs and failures. She etched her knowledge and insights on her scales, giving her body a new shape, a magical frame that kept herself whole. Yluma’s careful talons now shape the form of each arcane dragon, taking care to enshrine their essence within the patterns of their scales to make sure that they do not struggle as she struggled.

fields.text: Deity Yluma (The Living Page) Source Draconic Codex pg. 34 More than her kin, Yluma wielded magic with power. Magical currents coursed through her body, filling her frame with the power to raise mountains and level entire plains. Yet each awe-inspiring act came at an incredible cost. With each miraculous feat, Yluma’s form changed, becoming less distinct and whole. Yluma shared her fears with her father, but the Waybringer could do nothing to stop this change. He confided that in Yluma he could see a fragment of Sarshallatu’s infinity. Yluma’s body, no matter how powerful, would eventually be torn at the seams, unable to contain her mother’s unbound vastness. And so, Yluma vowed to seek out Sarshallatu, hoping that her mother would help her get rid of such a curse. She traveled far and wide across the edges of creation. Her frame, pulled and stretched by the trials she faced, seemed on the verge of collapse when she finally reached her mother’s lonely refuge. She gazed upon her divine mother, trying to take in all her vastness and power. Yluma looked at herself, feeling the soreness of her powerful muscles, tired and aching after the long journey. She traced the scars left by her battles, remembering how she bested all those who opposed her using her gifts. And she understood. So, she returned to her kin, her body a monument to her triumphs and failures. She etched her knowledge and insights on her scales, giving her body a new shape, a magical frame that kept herself whole. Yluma’s careful talons now shape the form of each arcane dragon, taking care to enshrine their essence within the patterns of their scales to make sure that they do not struggle as she struggled. **Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 132

Yog-Sothoth is, along with Azathoth, one of the greatest of the Outer Gods. In appearance, he is said to be a congeries of iridescent spheres—brilliant, foaming bubbles that constantly expand and collapse in upon themselves. He has other manifestations, however, including the Lurker on the Threshold, a mass of black tentacles that endlessly writhe, reach, and grow, and a mysterious humanoid figure hidden behind a shimmering veil.

 Yog-Sothoth embodies all of space and time; he exists in all places and in all moments simultaneously. Paradoxically, however, he is unable to manifest in the mortal universe unless summoned, a magical act that almost always results in untold destruction. He is known as the Key and the Gate, and magicians and cults research him in an effort to master time and space. Fortunately, his worship is not widespread, but some of those who have delved deep into his secrets describe him as an ambivalent figure, rather than a malevolent one, who guards cosmic secrets and makes them accessible to those who dare to ask for them. Yog-Sothoth reveals the true nature of the universe, but this is a thing that once seen cannot be unseen, and wise mortals turn aside from Yog-Sothoth’s offer of cosmic knowledge in favor of a more mundane existence.

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 312

Yrmidar is a [werebear](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3237) frost giant deity of shipbuilders, camaraderie, and the hunt. When in his giant form, he is depicted as a frost giant with long silver hair in a braid that reaches past the small of his back, snowwhite eyes, and sharp obsidian-black fingernails. In his hybrid form, which is his most common form, his head transforms into that of a polar bear and his fingernails grow to become a bear’s claws. In his werebear form, he becomes an enormous, bipedal polar bear with deadly fangs and claws. When he transforms into this beast, even the most battle-hardened of deities steer clear of him. Most mortals and gods alike consider this affliction a curse, but Yrmidar does not share that belief. To him and many of his followers, it is a power and a responsibility to be proud of and at peace with. 

Faith in Yrmidar is most popular among frost giant shipbuilders and hunters; however, he has garnered a significant following among the Ulfen people as well. Large settlements of the faithful tend to form near coastlines perfect for ports or forests ideal for hunting. They have such a tangible sense of togetherness between them that it can be rather unnerving for unaccustomed outsiders to witness. Yrmidar asks his followers to support one another, emphasizing the importance of community. His aphorism “Aid Happily, Accept Gratefully,” is often emblazoned beneath his religious symbol. Many hunting and sailing parties thank the Old Bear for helping bring them together, and in many cases, even directly leading to marriages.

fields.text: Deity Yrmidar (The Old Bear) Source Divine Mysteries pg. 312 Yrmidar is a werebear frost giant deity of shipbuilders, camaraderie, and the hunt. When in his giant form, he is depicted as a frost giant with long silver hair in a braid that reaches past the small of his back, snowwhite eyes, and sharp obsidian-black fingernails. In his hybrid form, which is his most common form, his head transforms into that of a polar bear and his fingernails grow to become a bear’s claws. In his werebear form, he becomes an enormous, bipedal polar bear with deadly fangs and claws. When he transforms into this beast, even the most battle-hardened of deities steer clear of him. Most mortals and gods alike consider this affliction a curse, but Yrmidar does not share that belief. To him and many of his followers, it is a power and a responsibility to be proud of and at peace with. Faith in Yrmidar is most popular among frost giant shipbuilders and hunters; however, he has garnered a significant following among the Ulfen people as well. Large settlements of the faithful tend to form near coastlines perfect for ports or forests ideal for hunting. They have such a tangible sense of togetherness between them that it can be rather unnerving for unaccustomed outsiders to witness. Yrmidar asks his followers to support one another, emphasizing the importance of community. His aphorism “Aid Happily, Accept Gratefully,” is often emblazoned beneath his religious symbol. Many hunting and sailing parties thank the Old Bear for helping bring them together, and in many cases, even directly leading to marriages. **Source** [Pathfinder #216: The Acropolis Pyre](/Sources.aspx?ID=271) pg. 76

 In an act of hypocrisy, Ongalte used her cyclopean powers to empower a lieutenant in her deicidal campaign:  a human pirate named Ytildos. He served Ongalte for years before she was wounded in battle, at which point he stole her wealth and left her to die. Ever since, Ytildos has plied Kartaji Bay, always on the lookout for plunder. When he can't find treasure, he makes it, seeding misinformation about the treacherous straits and reefs to sink ships and their cargo. His followers are equally opportunistic. However, their patron is fickle and greedy, and when he senses a worshipper's windfall, Ytildos often swoops in to demand a cut.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Zarongel](/Deities.aspx?ID=507)
(The Bark Breaker)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 312

Zarongel is the creator-god of [dog](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=392) killing, fire, and mounted combat. That [barghests](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=11) are profoundly dogshaped seems not to matter to either Zarongel or his followers. By all accounts, Zarongel appears to despise domesticated canines for becoming subservient to mortals. He’s often depicted as a wolf-like barghest with his hair composed of burning fire. His mouth drips a magma-like substance that mimics molten saliva. 

While not the strongest of the four creator-gods, Zarongel is surely the most agile one, with strong legs ready to hunt. He trained goblins to hunt dogs, creating a set of tactics involving arson specifically designed to leave them no escape route. Many [goblins](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=62) pass these canine hunting methods down through generations. According to Zarongel, once slain, a dog must be burnt away to fully eliminate them. Zarongel’s followers aim to leave no trace behind, keeping the few remaining bones for rituals and stews.

Zarongel doesn’t heed every prayer. Anyone looking to gain his attention must first burn a hunted dog. Goblins believe that anyone attempting to commune with Zarongel before accomplishing this trial results in bad luck for one hundred months. Those who manage to communicate with the Bark-Breaker typically earn the gift of a riding companion, typically a goblin dog or warg. Zarongel’s faithful are expected to be able to ride such beasts, though the god offers them no aid in this endeavor, and more than a few unlucky goblins have been eaten by their own god-sent mounts.

 A mythic sea hag, Zeaki offers transformative magic to all comers, and although she bears no malice toward these visitors, she nevertheless extracts a severe price for her services. Her island of Itia is home to countless unique beasts, each said to be some impolite visitor whom Zeaki transformed into a form more befitting their poor manners. Those who worship her— including witches of various patrons—seek personal change, mastery of magic, and control over the tides. The price Zeaki demands in return is unique to each follower and isn't always paid up front.

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 302

The Bitter Flame was originally forged by [Szuriel](/Deities.aspx?ID=136), the Rider of War, in her domain, the Cinder Furnace. She created Zelishkar as the embodiment of the funeral pyres that often follow in the wake of the wars she brings. The aggressive [daemonic](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=386) feline performed his duties so well that Szuriel promoted him to harbinger. Though Zelishkar continues to personify the most sadistic uses of fire, he holds a spark of resentment in his cores that he owes all that he is to Szuriel and schemes to someday supplant her. 

Zelishkar is shaped like a monstrous three-tongued [tiger](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2867) made of living crimson flames. His body is protected by a thin, durable cuirass crafted from obsidian. His eyes are jet black and emit a sinister orange glow.

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 304

Zevgavizeb, the Glutton in the Dark, is the demon lord of caverns, reptiles, and xulgaths. He dwells at the center of a massive network of caverns called Gluttondark, filled with continually warring nations of reptilian creatures, along with other, more hideous subterranean creatures. He encourages these conflicts to cull the weakest of his followers and devours all life found within defeated nations as a price for failure. Largely concerned with these perpetual conflicts, Zevgavizeb seldom seeks to influence Golarion directly, though reptilian ancestries and [xulgaths](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=486) in particular routinely commit atrocities in his name.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">
[Zipacna](/Deities.aspx?ID=604)
(The Mountain Below)
</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries Web Supplement](/Sources.aspx?ID=237) pg. 21

The lazy but violent Zipacna is one the largest sahkil tormentors, resembling a massive caiman with four eyes and unnervingly human hands. He prefers to lounge in the lusher regions of Xibalba being pampered by the unfortunate souls he’s forcefully inducted into his service, doling out vicious punishments when his demands aren’t met. Even the other sahkil tormentors avoid testing his fury, as his penchant for destructive violence overwhelms everything in his path.

Zipacna is worshipped by those who abuse their strength and power to take what they want, ranging from selfish warriors to irresponsible nobles. These acolytes never use their abilities to fulfill their responsibilities, only to indulge their petty desires at the expense of others. However, the indolent Zipacna is surprisingly efficient when he needs to be as sloppy work only leads to more work, which is a travesty in his eyes. Despite this, one is unlikely to witness Zipacna do any sort of work outside of acts of violence as his beleaguered servants tend to his every whim. It is said the last time the great caiman did so much as lift a stone was before the days of Azlant.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">
